summary: Reviewed ledger-store.test.ts (LedgerStore.renameSlug describe block) and api.test.ts (handleRenameProject tests). All test code is correct, well-isolated, and comprehensively covers the specified behaviors.

7 renameSlug storage tests confirmed: old-dir-gone/new-dir-exists, slug field updated, other fields preserved, same-slug guard, 3 invalid-slug inputs (spaces+special, path-traversal, empty), target-conflict guard, return value correctness.
updateTitle regression test uses strict toBe equality on last_updated before vs after — any inadvertent mutation would be caught.
API test count (7) exceeds spec requirement (5). Bonus tests add disk-level verification and last_updated preservation for the slug-rename path — both are meaningful regression guards.
No .skip, xit, or inactive tests found. All test cases active.
error message patterns in rejects.toThrow are appropriately loose (/already/i, /invalid/i, /already in use/i) — not brittle against minor message wording changes.
Full 1107-test Vitest suite passes with 0 failures, 36 files — no regressions from WP-001 or WP-002 changes.

comments.note: Test isolation is correct: each test in the describe block gets a fresh tempLedgerRoot via mkdtemp in beforeEach and full cleanup via rm(..., {recursive:true, force:true}) in afterEach. No shared mutable state between tests.

The target-conflict test correctly seeds the conflicting ledger dir using a separate LedgerStore instance and writeProjectMeta() rather than a raw fs.mkdir — guarantees a well-formed target directory that matches real-world scenarios.
'preserves other fields' test reads .meta.json raw JSON directly rather than through readProjectMeta() — stronger guarantee: proves no extra fields were silently added or removed by renameSlug().
No blocking observations — test file is well-structured, coverage is thorough, and the bonus API tests are genuine regression value.
